title: Crowding-Out or Crowding-In? The Effects of Idea Evaluation on Evaluators' Idea Generation
authors: Johanna Schnier; Christina Raasch; Tim G. Schweisfurth
eligible_reason: Not a staggered-adoption design. The treatment eval_w is a recurring exposure indicator (1 during the seven days after an employee evaluates an idea, 0 otherwise; rolling 7-day max of a daily evaluation flag) that switches on and off many times per employee, so there are no unit-specific adoption dates or cohorts in Hull's sense; dropping switched-off periods would discard the identifying within-employee variation. The main-text estimators are logit and Poisson with choice-based-sampling weights (Tables 1-2, Figure 3), OLS with continuous topic-familiarity shares (Table 3), and idea-level OLS (Table 4). The dCDH did_multiplegt_dyn robustness (Table A.9, Figure A.5) is appendix-only and applied to the same non-absorbing treatment. In addition, the package ships only synthetic (randomly generated) data, so no estimate can be replicated.
design_notes: Employee-day panel from a multinational firm's idea management system; choice-based sample of employee-days (weights). Outcome sub = 1 if the employee submitted an idea that day; num_sub count. Treatment eval_w = evaluated an idea within the past 7 days; lead/lag dummies -7..+7 relative to each evaluation. FE: employee_id + date, cluster employee_id. Mechanism tables use idea dyads (cosine similarity), familiarity shares, IV with reminders (Table A.24), CEM-matched sample (Table A.27), placebo shuffles (A.26).
main_or_robustness: main (DiD framing) but design is recurring exposure, not staggered adoption
n_adoption_cohorts_note: No adoption cohorts: treatment is a repeated 7-day window after each evaluation event.
modern_estimators_named: TwoWayFEWeights loaded (no call found in analysis scripts)

screener_notes: Clear exclusion on design (non-absorbing recurring treatment) and on data (synthetic). The ft_* hits come from the paper's discussion of heterogeneous-effects robustness (Table A.9).
